id: title:CShine612:stop repeating the same low reputation warning

observations.behavior: Replaces the timestamp in the email campaign key with an ISO week string for LOW findings while retaining it for HIGH findings.
observations.posthog_connection: This change prevents duplicate emails from being sent to recipients when a low-severity reputation warning reappears within the same calendar week. It could reduce alert fatigue and unnecessary database writes associated with repeated task dispatches.

observations.behavior: Adds unit tests asserting that two calls with timestamps falling in different weeks produce separate messages, while two calls in the same week share one message; also checks that high-impact events are not deduplicated by this rule.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides regression protection against regressions or incorrect behavior of the new deduplication logic, supporting reliability and maintenance rather than adding production capability.

observations.limitations: The implementation is localized to a single helper function and its test coverage. No broader system dependency or shared infrastructure changes are shown. The tier does not demonstrate systemic risk reduction or broad reach.

review.limitations: The implementation is localized to a single helper function and its test coverage. No broader system dependency or shared infrastructure changes are shown. The tier does not demonstrate systemic risk reduction or broad reach.
review.reason: Narrow, bounded improvement: adds per-week deduplication for specific low-impact email notifications without changing wider workflows or introducing critical-path dependencies.
review.posthog_relevance: Could help PostHog users receive fewer redundant alerts about transient low-severity issues, potentially reducing noise and minor operational overhead.
review.uncertainty: None; all relevant hunks are complete and self-contained.
